n: Oliver tried to translate but did not succeed, and went back to being Joseph’s scribe. The Lord tenderly calls him “my son” and asks him to keep writing until the Book of Mormon is finished.

f.g: a term of affection and covenant relationship, not a rebuke.

n: Oliver will have power to help translate other records in the future.
Oliver should be patient; it isn’t wise for him to translate right now.

f.g: suitable or advisable at the time.

n: His present calling is to be Joseph’s scribe — important work in its own right.
Oliver lost the privilege because he didn’t continue as he had begun.
Oliver should not complain; the Lord has handled this wisely.
Oliver’s mistake: he assumed God would simply hand him the translation when all he did was ask. Revelation usually requires effort on our part.

f.w: you took no thought save it was to ask me

n: A central teaching on personal revelation: study it out in your mind, reach a conclusion, then ask God if it is right. If it is, he will cause your bosom to “burn” — a feeling of confirmation.

f.w: study it out in your mind
your bosom shall burn within you

n: If it is not right, you will feel no such confirmation but a “stupor of thought” — a confused, foggy feeling that makes the wrong idea slip away.

f.g: mental dullness or confusion; an inability to hold onto the idea.

n: Had Oliver understood this process, he could have translated — but now is not the time.
The opportunity was right when he began, but fear got in the way, and the moment has passed.
Joseph has been given enough strength to carry on, so the work is not harmed. The Lord gently adds that he condemns neither of them.

f.w: neither of you have I condemned

n: If Oliver does what he’s been asked, he will prosper. He must stay faithful and resist temptation.
Stand firm in your calling, and not a hair of your head will be lost; you will be lifted up at the last day.

f.w: a hair of your head shall not be lost
lifted up at the last day
